kzig 0.3.0 gives the app's mode a kzig name: **`KZIG_ENV`**. Requires Zig 0.17.0. Pre-alpha: APIs will change.

## Highlights

- **`KZIG_ENV`** says how the app runs: `development`, `test`, or anything else (unset included) for production. It turns on `dev_defaults`, the migrations-at-boot policy, and Swagger with `disable_in_prod`. `NODE_ENV` is still read when `KZIG_ENV` isn't set, so KickJS `.env` files and deployment configs keep working; `KZIG_ENV` wins when both are set.
- **`Process.env`**: inject `*const kzig.Process` and read `.development`, `.@"test"` or `.production` (`dev_or_test` is still there).
- **`kzig new`**: the scaffolded `Config` no longer has a `node_env` field that defaulted to `development` while the app ran as production, and its tests boot with `KZIG_ENV=test`.
- **Releases** now get their notes from `scripts/release-notes.sh`: hand-written highlights from `.github/release-notes/<tag>.md`, then the commits since the last tag. [RELEASING.md](https://github.com/forinda/kzig/blob/main/RELEASING.md) documents the flow.

## Changes to note when upgrading

- `kzig dev` and `kzig start` set `KZIG_ENV` (to `development` / `production`) instead of `NODE_ENV`, and only when neither is set. If your own `Config` reads a `node_env` field, either set `NODE_ENV` yourself or read `Process.env` instead.
